To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Finnish food banks are in a unique position in the world, in the sense that they are not only the only food banks in Finland, but also that they have developed a very unique model for food distribution.

1) the Finnish food aid sector is dominated by the state; 2) there is a lack of participatory alternatives for charity work; 3) food aid is a part of the social safety net; 4) food aid is not an alternative to the social safety net but a supplement to it; and 5) there is a need to develop the social safety net in order to reduce the demand for charity food aid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of food donation practices and the ways in which the Finnish food donation system has developed.
the development of Finnish charitable food delivery, its relationship to the international development of the field, and the potential of the Finnish development for other countries.

the Finnish charity food delivery system has been developed in a way that has made it possible to create a system that can be considered participatory in the sense that the system is based on the participation of the recipients and the food donors.

Finnish food charity is in the process of change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach to the study of charity food delivery.
we have been able to demonstrate how the Finnish food charity sector is in the process of developing in a direction that is more inclusive and participatory.
it is possible to create participatory and sustainable food donation systems, but that it takes time and effort.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to develop the concept of food charity in a way that is more inclusive and participatory.

the Finnish model of charity food delivery is unique in the international comparison, and that the Finnish model is not only a result of the Finnish food culture and history, but also of the Finnish welfare state and the social policy system.
